name: Latvia

flag.description: A dark carmine-red field divided by a narrow white horizontal stripe in the middle, in the ratio 2:1:2.
flag.symbolism: Legend tells of a wounded leader wrapped in a white sheet whose blood stained its edges; the dark red stands for readiness to give one's life for freedom.

hook: Latvia's 'Latvian red' is nearly maroon and its white stripe is thin; Austria's is bright red with three equal stripes.
trivia: A red-white-red banner is mentioned in the 13th-century Livonian Rhymed Chronicle, making it one of the oldest flag designs in the world.
Banned under Soviet rule, the flag was officially restored in February 1990.
